subject: Urgent: Orchid Health regional cascade — summary + CTO briefing
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@orchidhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Torres <lydia@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T08:12:00Z
Subject: Production 5xx and latency spike in us-east-1 AZ-3

Priyom —

We just started seeing a large number of 5xx responses and slow responses (~p95=2.4s, p99 spike to 5s) for our API traffic routed through us-east-1 AZ-3. Errors started ~07:58 UTC and haven't fully subsided. We pushed a warm cache and retried, but errors persist. Our customers are seeing request failures and timeouts across sessions.

This is impacting multiple teams here; we're on a call with our ops and product. Can you confirm whether you're seeing a regional problem and what the next steps are? Our account contact is Lydia and I'm happy to provide logs (attached a sample). This is P0 for us.

Samir
CTO (Orchid Health)

Attachments: orchid-502-sample.log, orchid-5xx-screenshot.png

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Lydia Torres <lydia@orchidhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Production 5xx and latency spike in us-east-1 AZ-3

Samir —

Thanks for the heads up and for the log dump. I'm escalating to SRE and our on-call ops now (cc'ed Hannah). We're treating this as P0 and will provide continual updates. First asks: can you confirm approximate traffic volume (rps) during the spike and whether you observed a change in request mix? Any recent config changes on your side?

Immediate steps from our side:
- Hannah will validate whether the issue is isolated to AZ-3 and confirm cross-region routing behavior.
- We'll check autoscaler activity and backend CPU/GPU saturation for any candidate hosts.
- If needed we'll shift traffic to a warm pool in us-east-1/secondary region to reduce client impact.

I'll run point with you until we have a recovery plan.

— Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Production 5xx and latency spike in us-east-1 AZ-3

Priyom / Marissa —

Initial triage summary (06:58–09:00 UTC):
- We observed an abrupt increase in 5xx rate originating from a subset of inference workers pinned to us-east-1 AZ-3. Error rate peaked at ~12% for the customer’s routes between 07:58–08:25 UTC.
- p50/p95/p99 for Orchid's routes: 120ms / 2.6s / 5.8s during the window. Baseline p95 is ~180ms.
- Autoscaler triggered scale-up attempts but many containers failed initialization due to a kernel-level network device error on a host pool; the failed initializations caused request retries and cascading timeout amplification.
- Traffic was automatically redistributed to us-east-1 AZ-1 and eu-west-1 for short windows; eu-west-1 saw a 30% increase in load and transient elevated latencies.

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Quarantined affected host pool and drained traffic from AZ-3 hosts to healthy pools (manual drain + affinity override).
2) Rolled out a soft routing rule to prefer AZ-1/us-east-1 and limit cross-region fallback to eu-west-1 for Orchid traffic.
3) Disabled a suspect provisioning hook that was failing on initialization (temporary rollback).
4) Warmed a small group of standby workers with Orchid models to reduce cold-start spike.

Current status (09:03 UTC): error rate reduced to ~1.5% on Orchid's routes; p95 now ~420ms. We're keeping a 10m monitoring cadence.

Open actions for remediation and postmortem:
- Investigate kernel NIC errors on the failed hosts (ticketing infra team).
- Audit autoscaler health checks to ensure retries don't amplify timeouts under partial host failures.
- Validate KV cache integrity; there are signs of stale cache invalidations during drained failovers.

I'll prepare a short CTO briefing with the timeline and ask for exec approval for credits for impact if Orchid requests.

— Hannah
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T12:15:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Re: Production 5xx and latency spike in us-east-1 AZ-3

Rishi —

Forwarding thread and initial findings. SRE isolated host-level NIC flaps causing multiple worker init failures; autoscaler retry behaviour amplified the outage as failed inits consumed capacity and caused retries. We contained and warmed standby capacity; Orchid is asking for an exec-level briefing and possible credits.

Proposed exec asks:
- Approve a customer goodwill credit equal to 10% of last month's usage while we complete the postmortem.
- Approve a formal postmortem with Orchid, scheduled within 72 hours.
- Sanction a limited hotfix window for autoscaler health-check changes (risk: small config change to reduce retry aggressiveness).

TL;DR impact: multi-tenant regional disruption for a high-value account, customer-visible errors and latency. Recommendation is to approve the credit (10%) and commit to postmortem timeline.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Production 5xx and latency spike in us-east-1 AZ-3

Thanks for the rapid containment. I agree with Marissa's proposed path. Approvals:
- Approve the 10% goodwill credit for Orchid for last month's usage (finance to process).
- Approve postmortem meeting within 72 hours and a customer-facing timeline. Priyom, please own the customer comms and confirm slot availability.
- Approve the limited autoscaler health-check hotfix; Hannah, ensure we have rollback steps and a safety window.

Also ask engineering infra to prioritize a hardware-health sweep of hosts in us-east-1 AZ-3 and to provide a remediation ETA. Please include an interim note for the C-suite to show we have a mitigation and timeline.

Rishi
VP, Reliability & Infrastructure

From: Samir Patel <samir@orchidhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Torres <lydia@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T15:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Production 5xx and latency spike in us-east-1 AZ-3

Priyom —

Appreciate the fast response and the containment. The Orchid teams confirm service quality has returned to acceptable levels and we've stopped seeing customer-visible failures. We accept the proposed postmortem and the 72-hour window; please include the detailed timeline and the corrective actions you listed (autoscaler fix, host sweep, KV cache validation).

As a follow-up: we expect a formal note for our procurement and legal teams documenting the credit and the remediation plan; if that isn't provided we'll need to escalate through our account procurement channel. We'll await the postmortem invite.

Thanks,
Samir
CTO, Orchid Health

Attachments referenced: orchid-multipage-mtp.pdf (mutual action plan template)
